quote: return [];  // storage blocked or corrupt: start empty; app.js tells the user
title: Corrupt or unreadable saved data loads as an empty list, nothing tells the user, and the next save overwrites it
evidence: The comment says app.js tells the user. app.js never does: it calls loadRecipes() at line 3 and renders the empty state. The filter at store.js:7 also drops any record without a string name, with no notice. Driven: corrupt JSON '{bad' showed 'No recipes yet', status was empty, and adding one recipe replaced the stored value with only that recipe. A stored record {id:'2',title:'B'} was gone after the next add.
failing_case: Saved value is damaged (or holds a record from another version with a different name field). The page opens as a first run. The user adds one recipe, and the old data is permanently overwritten. The user was never told anything was wrong.
remediation: Return a result that says it failed or dropped records, show it in the status area, and keep the raw value under a backup key before the first overwrite. Store a version with the data.

title: Each tab saves its own in-memory list over the whole stored list, so a second tab erases the first tab's recipes
evidence: app.js:3 reads storage once; every save writes the whole array. There is no 'storage' event handler and no re-read before writing. Driven: two tabs opened on the same empty store, one adds FromA, the other adds FromC; a third tab then lists only FromC.
failing_case: Open the app in two tabs. Add a recipe in tab 1, then add another in tab 2 without reloading. Reload: only tab 2's recipe is left. Tab 1's recipe was reported as 'Saved'.
remediation: Re-read the stored list immediately before each change and apply the change to that, and listen for the 'storage' event to refresh the view.

title: Delete shows "Deleted" when the save failed; the recipe comes back on reload
evidence: saveRecipes returns false on failure (store.js:13-20). The add handler checks it (app.js:24-25); the delete handler drops the result and writes the success message at app.js:36. Driven in Chromium with setItem forced to throw QuotaExceededError.
failing_case: Storage is full or blocked. The user deletes recipe A and confirms. The status says Deleted “A”. localStorage still holds A, so a reload brings it back with no warning.
remediation: Check the return value of saveRecipes in the delete handler and show the same kind of failure message as the add handler. Decide whether to keep the in-memory removal or roll it back.

quote: return Array.isArray(data) ? data.filter((r) => r && typeof r.name === "string") : [];
title: Loaded records are only checked for a name, so a missing id makes Delete throw and a non-number minutes breaks the total
evidence: app.js:10 renders data-id="undefined" for a record with no id; app.js:32 find() then returns undefined and describe(r) at line 33 throws (the comment at app.js:14 says it is never null). totalMinutes (store.js:23) adds r.minutes without a type check. Driven with stored [{name:'Soup',minutes:'30'},{name:'Pie',minutes:20}]: after adding Tea (5) the status read 'Total cooking time: 030205 minutes.' and clicking Delete on Soup threw 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading name)' and nothing was removed.
failing_case: Storage holds a record saved without an id or with minutes as a string (any earlier shape, or a hand edit). The total shows string-joined digits or NaN, and that recipe can never be deleted.
remediation: Normalise each record at load: require a string id (assign one if missing), coerce minutes to a finite positive number, and drop or flag what cannot be fixed. Guard r === undefined in the delete handler.

requirement.why: saved data from an earlier version or manual edit; nothing in the repo states the history of the stored shape

title: After Delete the focused button is destroyed and focus falls to the page body
evidence: render() replaces list.innerHTML (app.js:10). Driven: after confirming a delete, document.activeElement was BODY. The status line is announced, but a keyboard user starts again from the top of the page.
failing_case: Keyboard user tabs to the third Delete button, presses Enter, confirms. Focus resets to the document start; to delete the next recipe they must tab through the heading and form again (WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order).
remediation: After removal, move focus to the next Delete button, or the previous one, or the Your recipes heading (tabindex=-1) when the list is empty.
